tabs.label: Q2 Exec Summary
tabs.headline: Q2 FY27 lands short of plan on every growth measure

semantic.definition: ACV booked on net-new-logo closed-won opportunities, excluding expansion and renewal, at fiscal-quarter grain.
semantic.rls: Analytics BU hierarchy — viewer sees only their branch
semantic.why: Net-new is the one measure that cannot be reconstructed from opportunity records alone — it depends on a governed first-purchase test against account history.

directMode.missing: A governed net-new-logo test — Org62 offers a manually-maintained Type picklist, a New_Logo__c checkbox, and a first-close-date derivation that disagree
directMode.effect: Three defensible NNAOV values with no arbiter, so the -75% Y/Y read cannot be defended in the room
directMode.thesis: Metric definitions live in the analysis layer, not in raw data — a CRM can host competing candidate fields but cannot rule between them.
directMode.risk: Present a headline decline that is off by up to 87% and call it settled
directMode.trustCost: A confident wrong number costs more trust than a flagged unknown

semantic.definition: Annualized contract value on closed-won opportunities, normalized to a 12-month term, net of ramp and multi-year discounting.
semantic.grain: Fiscal quarter × Business unit × Product motion
semantic.rls: Analytics BU hierarchy — viewer sees only their branch
semantic.why: This is the same certified ACV measure the Five Year Trend tab resolves against — which is why the two tabs reconcile rather than merely look similar.

directMode.missing: A governed ACV formula — Amount, Tableau_Amount__c, Analytics_Amount__c, and AmountConverted__c all coexist on Opportunity with no defined winner
directMode.effect: The $82M headline moves by $22M depending on which Amount column the query author reaches for
directMode.thesis: Metric definitions live in the analysis layer, not in raw data — a CRM can host competing candidate fields but cannot rule between them.
directMode.risk: Two teams present two different ACV numbers for the same quarter in the same week
directMode.trustCost: Every downstream number that divides by ACV inherits the ambiguity

metrics.caption: Four candidate Amount columns, no defined winner
Falling year over year, still over plan

semantic.definition: ACV lost to non-renewal and downsell in the period, measured against the prior-period contract book. Lower is better; the certified measure carries that polarity.
semantic.rls: Analytics BU hierarchy — viewer sees only their branch
semantic.why: Polarity is part of the certified definition. Because the measure declares lower-is-better, 104% of plan renders as over-plan churn automatically — nobody has to remember to color that cell differently by hand.
semantic.polarityNote: Slide-level color coding is applied by the deck author. Here the direction of good comes from the measure itself, so -12% Y/Y reads positive and 104% of plan reads as a miss.

directMode.missing: A point-in-time contract book — Org62 stores current contract state, not the prior-period snapshot attrition is measured against
directMode.effect: Attrition has to be rebuilt by hand from history objects each quarter, and the polarity is whatever the deck author decides to color it
directMode.thesis: Time-aware context has to be mediated by a semantic layer — a system of record holds the present, not the comparison.
directMode.risk: Rebuild the number differently each quarter and read a trend that is really a methodology change
directMode.trustCost: A trend line nobody can reproduce is not a trend line

metrics.caption: No point-in-time contract book to measure against
Closest to plan of the four

semantic.definition: ACV of opportunities that entered a qualified stage during the period, counted at first qualification and never recounted on later stage moves.
semantic.rls: Analytics BU hierarchy — viewer sees only their branch
semantic.why: The never-recount rule is the whole measure. Without it, an opportunity that moves backward and forward through qualification inflates pipegen every time it crosses the line.

directMode.missing: The never-recount-on-re-entry rule — Org62 has CreatedDate and stage history, but no governed statement of which crossing counts
directMode.effect: Workable, but the number silently inflates whenever an opportunity bounces back through qualification
directMode.thesis: Business rules that shape a measure are the measure — leaving them in query code means every author reimplements them slightly differently.
directMode.risk: Report pipeline coverage that is inflated by re-entries and plan against it
directMode.trustCost: Ungoverned but usable — the tier where errors are quiet rather than loud

metrics.caption: Stage re-entry rule left to the query author

portlets.label: ACV by product motion
portlets.sublabel: Embedded is growing into a shrinking base

metrics.insight: Embedded is now 29% of Q2 ACV, up from 14% a year ago — but it is taking share of a base that shrank 28%. The mix is rotating faster than the total is falling.
metrics.caption: $82M total · Embedded share 29%

semantic.definition: Certified ACV split by the product-motion grouping that maps every SKU to exactly one of Embedded or Agentic.
semantic.rls: Analytics BU hierarchy — viewer sees only their branch
semantic.why: The split adds to the same certified $82M as the ACV tile above because both resolve to one measure. The mix insight only exists because the SKU-to-motion mapping is governed rather than re-derived per deck.

directMode.missing: The SKU-to-motion taxonomy — Org62 stores product codes, not the Embedded / Agentic grouping the business reasons in
directMode.effect: The split cannot be produced at all, so the mix-rotation insight disappears rather than degrades
directMode.thesis: Business vocabulary is an asset that has to live somewhere shared — otherwise every analysis rebuilds the same grouping by hand, slightly differently.
directMode.risk: Miss that Embedded nearly doubled its share while the base fell
directMode.trustCost: The insight is not wrong, it is absent — the most expensive failure mode

metrics.insight: Without a governed SKU-to-motion taxonomy there is no Embedded / Agentic split to report — only an undifferentiated $82M.

rules.title: Flow vs stock
rules.body: A flow accumulates across a period, so FY27 H1 is plotted detached and offered a run-rate ghost. A stock is a balance read at a point in time, so its H1 reading joins the line and is never annualised.

rules.title: Zero baseline
rules.body: Every value axis starts at zero. A padded baseline makes each decline look steeper, and at this size nobody would notice it had been truncated.

rules.title: Polarity
rules.body: Direction of good comes from the measure. Attrition declares lower-is-better, so its falling H1 figure reads as the only good news on the tab without anyone recolouring a cell.

rules.title: Colour threshold
rules.body: Movements inside ±10% render amber, beyond it red or green — one stated threshold rather than a per-cell judgement.

semantic.definition: The comparability, scaling, polarity and threshold rules the semantic layer applies to every measure on this tab.
semantic.grain: Applies to all measures on this tab
semantic.rls: Not scoped — rules apply to every viewer identically
semantic.why: These rules are the semantic layer doing its job. They are properties of the measures, so every chart, export and agent reading those measures inherits them — nobody has to remember to apply them, and nobody can quietly not.

candidates: rules live in each analyst's head
directMode.missing: Any place for a rule to live except the head of whoever built the chart
directMode.effect: Four rules that have to be remembered, re-explained and re-applied by every person and every agent that touches these numbers
directMode.thesis: Business rules that shape a measure are the measure — leaving them in query code means every author reimplements them slightly differently.
directMode.risk: Two analysts produce two defensible versions of the same tab
directMode.trustCost: Consistency becomes a matter of diligence rather than a property of the data
